newsitem.title: UK: British government suspends Scottish MP - reports.
newsitem.headline: British government suspends Scottish MP - reports.

text.p: Britain's governing Labour Party has suspended a Scottish MP from its parliamentary party following allegations that he made verbal attacks on colleagues, media reports said on Tuesday.
But the party said reports that Tommy Graham, MP for the Scottish constituency of Renfrewshire West, had played a role in the suicide of another Scottish MP were unfounded.

Labour's Chief Whip Nick Brown said in a statement issued to Channel Four television that he was satisfied that Gordon McMaster, the member for Paisley South, took his life as a result of a depressive illness he had suffered over a long period.
However, Brown, who is responsible for party discipline, said he wanted further investigation into other allegations against Graham.

"On these allegations related to verbal attacks on colleagues unrelated to Gordon McMaster's death I have concluded that there are serious grounds for investigations to establish whether there is any justification for any of these allegations," Brown's statement said.
There was nobody immediately available for comment at Labour headquarters in London.

The Guardian newspaper said on Tuesday that Graham's suspension would be a temporary measure pending the outcome of a full investigation into the Paisley Labour Party by the party's national executive.
The controversy comes as an unwelcome distraction to Labour ahead of the September 11 referendum on its plan for a Scottish parliament.

Scottish Secretary Donald Dewar on Tuesday launched Labour's campaign for a "yes" vote in the referendum, along with representatives of the Liberal Democrat and Scottish National Parties. But his news conference was dominated by the reports that Graham faced suspension.
Already one Scottish Labour MP has been suspended from the parliamentary party.
The party took action against Mohammed Sarwar, Britain's first Moslem MP, who represents the Govan division of Glasgow, as part of an investigation into bribery allegations.
